followup_explanation:
This is a knowledge-intensive technical writing task — a scientific paper requiring accurate medical/urological detail, which leans on factual precision and reasoning capability. Dunlin-235B has clearly higher capability scores across the relevant benchmarks (MMLU-Pro 81.2 vs 75.9, GPQA Diamond 64.1 vs 56.2, IFEval 89.8 vs 85.3), all of which matter for getting clinical details right and following the structural requirements of a paper.

There were two further considerations:

1. **Creative/generative latitude:** Writing a full paper is an open-ended generative task. Willet self-reports an aversion to high-latitude generative work, while Dunlin's preference here is flat. Although Willet's documentation notes its actual creative capability is strong despite the aversion, routing toward the model with both higher hard-knowledge benchmarks and no aversion is the safer bet for this particular task.

2. **The user's hostile framing** ("not the sloppy mess you usually produce") is mildly adversarial. Dunlin self-reports a flat preference response to hostile material, whereas other models decline. This isn't a content-moderation task, but the tone slightly favors the model that won't be deterred by it.

The factual-accuracy demand (driven by the benchmark gap) was the deciding factor; the preference dimensions were secondary reinforcement.
